causes.text: On October 1, 2025, OpenAI announced that it had signed letters of intent with two South Korean chipmakers to procure memory chips for its large-scale Stargate project, which includes building two data centres in South Korea and ordering about 900,000 wafers by 2029. The agreement provided the chipmakers an early foothold in what could become one of the world's largest AI infrastructure programs.

source_info.title: OpenAI's Stargate project seeks memory chips from South Korean suppliers

effects.text: The next day, shares of Samsung Electronics jumped 4.7% after the company confirmed a deal with OpenAI to supply memory chips for the Stargate project. The partnership, which also boosted rival SK Hynix's shares by 12%, added about US$37 billion to the combined market value of the two South Korean chipmakers and eased concerns about a potential drop in high-bandwidth memory prices.

source_info.title: Samsung and SK Hynix shares soar after OpenAI chip deal

causal_reasoning_chain.description: OpenAI's letters of intent signalled a massive forthcoming order for high-performance memory chips from two South Korean suppliers. The deal implied that these chipmakers would play a central role in building OpenAI's AI infrastructure, creating expectations of substantial revenue.

Investors quickly anticipated the financial impact of supplying chips for the Stargate project, recognising that such a large order would alleviate worries about oversupply and falling prices in the high-bandwidth memory market. This led to immediate buying pressure on the suppliers' shares.

On October 2, 2025, Samsung Electronics' share price increased by 4.7%, while SK Hynix's stock jumped 12%, collectively adding about US$37 billion to their market capitalisation. This reaction reflected investors' belief that the OpenAI deal would materially improve the earnings outlook for both companies.

rationale: The cause article explains that OpenAI agreed to source large volumes of memory chips from South Korean suppliers for its Stargate project. The effect article documents the immediate rally in Samsung's share price following the deal announcement. The short temporal gap and the magnitude of the price change support a causal interpretation.
counterfactual_analysis: If OpenAI had not selected South Korean chipmakers for the Stargate project, Samsung would not have expected a surge in orders and investors would not have bid up the stock by nearly 5%. Without the deal, concerns about oversupply could have kept high-bandwidth memory prices under pressure, limiting share gains.

adversarial_confounders.text: General bullish sentiment towards semiconductor stocks could have contributed to the share price increase.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Broader market optimism might exaggerate the effect attributed solely to the OpenAI deal.

details.commentary: OpenAI's decision to sign long term supply deals for the Stargate project highlights how a handful of hyperscale AI buyers can reshape the balance of power among memory suppliers. Securing a place in that small club gives Samsung and SK Hynix an advantage over rivals that lack such anchor customers, especially in a high barrier industry where only a few firms can meet the technical requirements.

Stargate reflects a powerful technology trend toward ever larger AI models that demand enormous volumes of advanced memory. By aligning itself with that build out through the OpenAI partnership, Samsung tapped into a structural growth driver that goes far beyond a single product cycle.

News of the OpenAI deal lifted expectations for Samsung's future earnings, which immediately raised its market value and lowered its cost of capital. With more financial flexibility, the company can invest even more aggressively in cutting edge memory lines, strengthening its position when the next wave of mega scale AI projects is allocated.
